react_result.final_narrative_text: The seven-metabolite differential signature converges on two primary biological axes. The cross-paradigm consensus winner is Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00043 / KEGG:hsa00052 / MUMM:galactose_metabolism), detected by all three independent enrichment paradigms with extraordinary statistical weight: run_ramp_enrichment reports FDR=4.25e-11 and fold-enrichment 1162× (four metabolites: sucrose, myo-inositol, galactinol, glycerol), run_metaboanalystr_psea reports p=3.25e-07 on the KEGG hsa00052 namespace, and run_mummichog reports p=8.4e-05 with 12 of 13 pathway metabolites matched in the human_mfn empirical network. The four confirmed carbohydrate members are structurally coherent: sucrose is the upstream disaccharide entering the Leloir pathway, myo-inositol and galactinol are direct galactose-branch intermediates, and glycerol is the shared terminal catabolite of all hexose tributaries. The second axis is glycerophospholipid metabolism (WP:WP2533, REACT:R-HSA-1483257, MUMM:glycerophospholipid_metabolism), where glycerol and myo-inositol together scaffold phosphatidylinositol head-group biosynthesis. A disease-context hit also appears: fructose 1-phosphate maps to Hereditary fructose intolerance (REACT:R-HSA-5657560, FDR=7.1e-4), where aldolase B deficiency causes toxic accumulation of this phosphorylated intermediate — the same metabolic logic (impaired sugar-phosphate catabolism → toxic intermediate build-up) that links galactosemia to the carbohydrate branch. Deoxycytidine anchors a Pyrimidine metabolism signal (KEGG:hsa00240, p=0.117) as a marginal contributor to the pyrimidine salvage axis. Overall the treatment perturbation most strongly dysregulates galactose / hexose carbon flux and, secondarily, membrane phospholipid head-group biosynthesis, with a secondary fructose-phosphate stress signature.

react_result.final_narrative_text: The seven-metabolite differential signature converges on galactose metabolism as the dominant pathway axis. run_ramp_enrichment reports Galactose Metabolism as the top hit (SMPDB:SMP00043, KEGG:map00052) with FDR=4.25e-11, 4 metabolites matched (sucrose, myo-inositol, galactinol, glycerol), fold-enrichment 1162x. run_metaboanalystr_psea independently confirms KEGG:hsa00052 (p=3.25e-07) with the same four compounds. run_mummichog identifies Galactose metabolism (MUMM:galactose_metabolism, p=6.72e-04) with 12 of 13 pathway metabolites matched in the human_mfn network. All three paradigms agree on the primary driver set: sucrose, myo-inositol, galactinol, and glycerol. A secondary axis of glycerophospholipid metabolism (MUMM:glycerophospholipid_metabolism, p=1.26e-03) is captured by mummichog, linking glycerol and myo-inositol to membrane lipid precursor pools. Fructose 1-phosphate maps to glycolysis (REACT:R-HSA-70171, FDR=9.77e-05) via the aldolase reaction, while deoxycytidine is a marginal contributor to pyrimidine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00240, p=0.117). Starch and Sucrose Metabolism (MUMM:starch_and_sucrose_metabolism, p=2.52e-04) provides a secondary mummichog hit that includes all seven input metabolites.

The four confirmed carbohydrate members are structurally coherent: sucrose is the upstream disaccharide entering the Leloir pathway, myo-inositol and galactinol are direct galactose-branch intermediates, and glycerol is the shared terminal catabolite of all hexose tributaries. The second axis is glycerophospholipid metabolism (WP:WP2533, REACT:R-HSA-1483257, MUMM:glycerophospholipid_metabolism), where glycerol and myo-inositol together scaffold phosphatidylinositol head-group biosynthesis. Deoxycytidine anchors a Pyrimidine metabolism signal (KEGG:hsa00240, p=0.117) as a marginal contributor to the pyrimidine salvage axis. The cross-paradigm consensus winner is Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00043 / KEGG:hsa00052 / MUMM:galactose_metabolism), detected by all three independent enrichment paradigms with extraordinary statistical weight: run_ramp_enrichment reports FDR=4.25e-11 and fold-enrichment 1162× (four metabolites: sucrose, myo-inositol, galactinol, glycerol), run_metaboanalystr_psea reports p=3.25e-07 on the KEGG hsa00052 namespace, and run_mummichog reports p=8.4e-05 with 12 of 13 pathway metabolites matched in the human_mfn empirical network. The four confirmed carbohydrate members are structurally coherent: sucrose is the upstream disaccharide entering the Leloir pathway, myo-inositol and galactinol are direct galactose-branch intermediates, and glycerol is the shared terminal catabolite of all hexose tributaries. The second axis is glycerophospholipid metabolism (WP:WP2533, REACT:R-HSA-1483257, MUMM:glycerophospholipid_metabolism), where glycerol and myo-inositol together scaffold phosphatidylinositol head-group biosynthesis. A disease-context hit also appears: fructose 1-phosphate maps to Hereditary fructose intolerance (REACT:R-HSA-5657560, FDR=7.1e-4), where aldolase B deficiency causes toxic accumulation of this phosphorylated intermediate — the same metabolic logic (impaired sugar-phosphate catabolism → toxic intermediate build-up) that links galactosemia to the carbohydrate branch. Deoxycytidine anchors a Pyrimidine metabolism signal (KEGG:hsa00240, p=0.117) as a marginal contributor to the pyrimidine salvage axis. Overall the treatment perturbation most strongly dysregulates galactose / hexose carbon flux and, secondarily, membrane phospholipid head-group biosynthesis, with a secondary fructose-phosphate stress signature.
